questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why rhinos have thick skin
A breeding programme to save the northern white rhino
How rhinos are protected from hunters in Kenya
The differences between northern and southern rhinos
questions.why: They discuss an artificial breeding programme to save the northern white rhino from extinction.

options: The first rhino embryo was born
Najin and Fatu were moved to Berlin
The breeding programme ended
Suni, the second-to-last male, died
questions.why: Neil says the species was close to extinction when Suni, the second-to-last male, died in 2014.

questions.q: What is happening to the five embryos now?
options: They are frozen until they can be put into southern rhinos
They have already been born and are living in Kenya
They are being grown into calves in a laboratory in Germany
They were implanted in Najin and Fatu last month
questions.why: Sam says they're being frozen until they can be implanted in southern rhinos.

questions.q: According to Thomas Hildebrandt, what is special about the embryos?
options: They are hybrids of northern and southern white rhinos
They come from parents that are closely related
They are pure northern white rhino with no inbreeding
They are all male, so they cannot have babies
questions.why: He says they're not hybrids but pure northern white rhino embryos with no inbreeding effect.

questions.q: Why does Thomas Hildebrandt say they 'desperately' need a calf soon?
options: Because the frozen embryos will soon stop working
So the old rhinos can teach it rhino behaviour
Because southern rhinos are also dying out
Because the programme will lose its money
questions.why: He says they can't preserve social knowledge, so the two rhinos must teach a new calf how to behave.

questions.q: How does this story connect to the 'nature versus nurture' debate?
options: Scientists want to change the rhinos' nature with new genes
The young rhinos won't need any nurture from other animals
Scientists can save the genes, but not the social learning
Nurture is only important for humans, not for animals
questions.why: Neil says they can preserve 'nature' but can't provide 'nurture' – the social knowledge.

questions.q: How long is a full rhino pregnancy?
options: 16 months
6 months
9 months
2 years
questions.why: Hildebrandt says a full pregnancy in a rhinoceros takes 16 months.

questions.q: What will the team look for before taking the next step?
options: The birth of a healthy southern rhino calf in the park
Official permission from the Kenyan government to continue
A new male northern white rhino found in the wild
The embryo implanting and forming a placenta
questions.why: He says if the embryo implants and forms a nice placenta, they'll proceed with the next step.
